title: Molecular epidemiological characteristics of H9N2 subtype avian influenza virus in the external environment of western Zhejiang, China, 2014–2025
abstract: Objective To elucidate the epidemiological distribution patterns of avian influenza virus (AIV) in the external environment of western Zhejiang from 2014 to 2025, analyze the molecular epidemiological characteristics of the H9N2 subtype, and assess its public health risks. Methods According to the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Program for Avian Influenza in Occupationally Exposed Populations and External Environments, real-time RT-PCR was used to detect AIV subtypes in environmental specimens. H9N2-positive samples with cycle threshold values <30 were inoculated into specific pathogen-free (SPF) embryonated chicken eggs for virus isolation, followed by whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis for phylogenetic and molecular characterization. Results A total of 7,762 specimens were tested from 2014 to 2025, with an overall positivity rate of 34.64% (2,689/7,762) for AIV. Significant differences in positivity rates were observed in seasons, regions, sampling sites, and specimen types (all p < 0.001). AIV activity peaked in winter and spring, with the highest rates detected in live poultry markets and chopping board swabs. The H9 was the predominant subtype, with co-circulation of multiple subtypes. All 48 H9N2 subtype isolates belonged to the G57 genotype, with the hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) genes falling into the Y280-like branch, while the internal genes exhibited a mosaic pattern combining G1-like and F/98-like lineages. Molecular characterization analysis revealed multiple mammalian adaptive mutations, involving alterations in receptor-binding sites (T163N, H191N, T197D, T198V, Q234L, Q235M), antigenic epitopes (D280G, N285S), and glycosylation sites (218NRTF, 313NCSK). NA stalk deletion (62–64 aa), along with multiple mutations in the hemadsorption site (E/K368N, D369S/G, D401G/V, N402D, W403L/R, Q432H). Additionally, multiple key amino acid substitutions were also identified in the internal proteins. Conclusion The external environment in western Zhejiang exhibits a high prevalence of AIVs with pronounced spatiotemporal clustering. H9 was the dominant subtype and co-circulated with multiple subtypes, with live poultry markets and slaughterhouses identified as high-risk settings. The H9N2 subtype AIV has accumulated multiple mammalian adaptive mutations, and exhibits genetic linkages across eastern Chinese provinces. These findings collectively underscore the need for an integrated One Health surveillance and early-warning system to reduce the risk of human infections with avian influenza.

title: Skuas as sentinels of high pathogenicity avian influenza H5N1 on the Antarctic Peninsula in the 2024/2025 austral summer
abstract: Despite Antarctica's geographic isolation, the first incursion of high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 was detected in the 2023/2024 austral summer. Surveillance for HPAI H5N1 in Antarctica remains patchy due to logistical, financial and infrastructure challenges, with many suspected cases remaining unconfirmed and few viral genome sequences available to date. Through the 2024/2025 austral summer, we undertook five sampling expeditions to the South Shetland Islands and Antarctic Peninsula facilitated by cruise ships/operators. Across more than 500 faecal environmental samples collected from apparently healthy penguins and marine mammals, we found no detectable evidence of HPAI H5N1. However, HPAI H5N1 was detected in all but one of the skua carcasses sampled, which, in most cases, were found within metres of penguin sub-colonies. All HPAI H5N1 viral genome sequences from skuas on the Antarctic Peninsula fell within a single lineage, which included those genomes from skuas sampled in the 2024/2025 season from the South Shetland Islands. Genomes were in a different clade to those from the Antarctic Peninsula collected in the 2023/2024 austral summer. Our results confirm that although the prevalence may be low, HPAI H5N1 is recurring in Antarctica, emphasizing the need for ongoing surveillance to monitor and mitigate threats to wildlife, even in the planet's most isolated regions.

title: APP and APLP2 Kunitz Domains Are Potent Endogenous Inhibitors of TMPRSS2 and Respiratory Virus Infection
abstract: Respiratory viruses depend on host proteases for activation of viral fusion proteins, making these enzymes attractive targets for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies. We previously identified Trypstatin, a human Bikunin-derived Kunitz domain, as a potent endogenous inhibitor of the airway serine protease TMPRSS2. Here, we investigated whether TMPRSS2 inhibition is shared by additional human Kunitz domains. Kunitz domains with high sequence similarity to Trypstatin were synthesized, refolded, and functionally characterized. Domains derived from amyloid precursor protein (APP) and amyloid precursor-like protein 2 (APLP2) potently inhibited TMPRSS2, with APP displaying subnanomolar activity comparable to camostat mesylate. APP and APLP2 selectively blocked SARS-CoV-2 Spike-mediated entry without affecting VSV-G-mediated entry or cell viability and inhibited infection by multiple coronaviruses and influenza viruses, but not TMPRSS2-independent rhinovirus. In primary human airway epithelial cultures, APP and Trypstatin reduced replication of SARS-CoV-2, endemic coronaviruses, and influenza A virus, and remained stable in airway mucus. These findings identify APP and APLP2 Kunitz domains as potent endogenous inhibitors of TMPRSS2-dependent respiratory virus infection and promising scaffolds for host-directed broad-spectrum antivirals.

title_zh: APP 和 APLP2 Kunitz 结构域是 TMPRSS2 和呼吸道病毒感染的有效内源抑制剂
source_body_en: Respiratory viruses depend on host proteases for activation of viral fusion proteins, making these enzymes attractive targets for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies. We previously identified Trypstatin, a human Bikunin-derived Kunitz domain, as a potent endogenous inhibitor of the airway serine protease TMPRSS2. Here, we investigated whether TMPRSS2 inhibition is shared by additional human Kunitz domains. Kunitz domains with high sequence similarity to Trypstatin were synthesized, refolded, and functionally characterized. Domains derived from amyloid precursor protein (APP) and amyloid precursor-like protein 2 (APLP2) potently inhibited TMPRSS2, with APP displaying subnanomolar activity comparable to camostat mesylate. APP and APLP2 selectively blocked SARS-CoV-2 Spike-mediated entry without affecting VSV-G-mediated entry or cell viability and inhibited infection by multiple coronaviruses and influenza viruses, but not TMPRSS2-independent rhinovirus. In primary human airway epithelial cultures, APP and Trypstatin reduced replication of SARS-CoV-2, endemic coronaviruses, and influenza A virus, and remained stable in airway mucus. These findings identify APP and APLP2 Kunitz domains as potent endogenous inhibitors of TMPRSS2-dependent respiratory virus infection and promising scaffolds for host-directed broad-spectrum antivirals.

title: Serovigilancia de influenza aviar H5N2 en patos y gansos domésticos de Río Blanco, San Marcos, Guatemala Serosurveillance of H5N2 avian influenza in domestic ducks and geese in Río Blanco, San Marcos, Guatemala Sorovigilância da influenza aviária H5N2 em patos e gansos domésticos de Río Blanco, San Marcos, Guatemala
abstract: Serological monitoring was conducted in domestic ducks and geese from the municipality of Río Blanco, San Marcos, in Guatemala’s western highlands. A total of 112 serum samples were taken from 83 Muscovy ducks (Cairina moschata) and 29 domestic geese (Anser anser var. domesticus) to determine the seroprevalence of H5N2 Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza (LPAI), by the haemagglutination inhibition test. A point seroprevalence of 0.89% was determined, with only 1 Muscovy duck out of 112 showing antibodies considered positive for the disease. The results indicate the presence of antibodies against H5N2 LPAI in a duck not vaccinated by the animal health service, suggesting exposure to the virus and possible circulation in the area. Therefore, it is necessary to remove obstacles to implement adequate surveillance and control strategies in the country.

title: Immunogenicity and Protective Efficacy of a Serum-Free Suspension MDCK Cell Culture-Based Inactivated H3N8 Avian Influenza Vaccine Compared with an Egg-Based Counterpart in Chickens
abstract: H3N8 subtype avian influenza virus (AIV) circulates in poultry with occasional zoonotic potential and vaccines are crucial for preventing and controlling avian influenza.Here, two inactivated vaccines were prepared against the H3N8 AIV with GD1102 as vaccine strain: an embryonated chicken egg-based vaccine (E-vac) and a serum-free suspension MDCK cell-based vaccine (C-vac).The efficacy of both vaccines was evaluated in specific pathogen-free chickens.All vaccinated groups and the challenge control were intranasally challenged with 10 6 EID50 of GD1102 at 14 days post-vaccination (dpv) while the negative control group received no challenge.HI antibody titers, viral shedding, tissue viral loads, and pathological lesions were systematically assessed.Both vaccines elicited robust humoral immune responses at 7 dpv and the C-vac group had significantly higher HI titers than the E-vac group (p 6 log2).Compared with the control group, both vaccines effectively reduced viral shedding and lessened histopathological lesions.These findings suggest that C-vac elicits a rapid antibody response and confers effective protection.Therefore, C-vac can be considered a promising new platform for H3N8 avian influenza vaccines.

full_text: Abstract Influenza A(H3N2) continues to pose a significant global public health challenge owing to its rapid antigenic evolution, particularly within the hemagglutinin (HA) glycoprotein, which frequently compromises vaccine effectiveness. The emergence of the H3N2 subclade K (J.2.4.1), characterized by multiple antigenically relevant mutations, necessitates the development of updated vaccine strategies capable of eliciting strain-specific immune responses. In this study, an immunoinformatics driven approach was employed to design a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) targeting the HA protein of the J.2.4.1 variant. The HA sequence was modified to incorporate lineage-specific mutations, and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and B-cell epitopes were predicted using the machine learning-based NetMHCpan/NetMHCIIpan algorithms and the IEDB platform. High-confidence epitopes were selected based on antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and immunogenic potential, and assembled using appropriate linkers with the 50S ribosomal protein L7/L12 as an adjuvant. The final MEV construct demonstrated favorable physicochemical characteristics, structural stability, and satisfactory model validation. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations revealed stable interactions between the vaccine construct and TLR4, while immune simulation predicted effective humoral and cellular immune responses with the generation of immunological memory. Population coverage analysis further indicated broad global applicability of the selected T-cell epitopes. Together, these findings suggest that the incorporation of J.2.4.1 specific antigenic mutations into the MEV may enhance strain-specific immune recognition and provide a promising computational framework for the rapid development of next-generation influenza vaccines. Nevertheless, experimental validation is required to confirm the immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy of the proposed vaccine candidate. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于血凝素 (HA) 糖蛋白中 进化 的快速抗原性,流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 造成了持续的公共卫生挑战,这经常破坏 疫苗 的有效性。具有多个抗原相关 突变 的 H3N2 亚支 K (J.2.4.1) 的出现需要更新的 疫苗 策略,能够引发毒株特异性 免疫应答。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用免疫信息学驱动的方法来设计针对 H3N2 亚进化枝 K (J.2.4.1) 变体的 HA 蛋白的多表位 疫苗 (MEV)。疫苗 构建体纳入了谱系特异性 突变,并对其理化性质、结构稳定性和 免疫应答 潜力进行了评估。
elements_zh.methods: HA 序列被修改为包括谱系特异性 突变,并使用 NetMHCpan/NetMHCIIpan 算法和 IEDB 平台预测细胞毒性 T 淋巴细胞 (CTL)、辅助 T 淋巴细胞 (HTL) 和 B 细胞表位。根据抗原性、非过敏性、无毒性和免疫原性潜力选择高置信度表位,然后与接头和 50S 核糖体蛋白 L7/L12 佐剂组装。
elements_zh.main_results: 最终的 MEV 构建体表现出良好的物理化学特性、结构稳定性和令人满意的模型验证。分子对接和动力学模拟显示与 TLR4 的稳定相互作用,而免疫模拟则预测了具有免疫记忆生成的有效体液和细胞 免疫应答。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为表明将 J.2.4.1 特异性抗原 疫苗 纳入 MEV 可能会增强毒株特异性免疫识别,为快速下一代流感 疫苗 开发提供有前景的计算框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项研究提供了一种计算策略,用于设计针对新兴变异的菌株特异性流感 疫苗,可能为未来的 监测 和 疫苗 菌株选择提供信息,以提高 疫苗 针对 H3N2 亚支 K 的有效性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于计算预测和模拟,作者明确指出需要实验验证来确认免疫原性、安全性和保护功效,这表明证据强度中等。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed a need to correct errors in previously published interaction data between RNA G-quadruplexes from influenza A virus vRNA and specific ligands, aiming to ensure the accuracy of reported parameters.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The correction pertains to a previously published study in PLOS One, focusing on the interaction of RNA G-quadruplexes from influenza A virus vRNA with TMPyP4 and BRACO-19 ligands.
analysis.methods: The correction involved re-evaluating and repositioning parameters obtained from isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements to align with the correct RNA oligomers and ligands, as originally reported in the retracted table.
analysis.main_results: The corrected Table 2 now accurately presents the parameters from ITC measurements, resolving the misalignment of data with the respective RNA oligomers and ligands.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The correction ensures the integrity of the original findings by rectifying errors in parameter assignment, thereby maintaining the validity of the reported interactions between influenza A virus RNA G-quadruplexes and the ligands studied.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Accurate reporting of these interactions is critical for advancing research into potential antiviral strategies targeting influenza A virus RNA structures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the nature of the correction, which addresses methodological reporting errors rather than introducing new experimental data or insights.

analysis.summary_en: This correction addresses errors in a previously published study on the interaction of RNA G-quadruplexes from influenza A virus vRNA with TMPyP4 and BRACO-19 ligands. The original errors involved misaligned parameters from isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements in Table 2. The corrected table now accurately reflects the interaction data, ensuring the integrity of the findings. While the correction does not introduce new experimental results, it is essential for maintaining the reliability of the reported interactions, which are relevant for potential antiviral research targeting influenza A virus RNA structures.

title: Sex-specific trajectories of adolescent brain maturation and sensorimotor gating after maternal influenza infection in mice
abstract: Maternal infection during pregnancy is increasingly recognised as a risk factor for neurodevelopmental disorders, yet how a clinically relevant viral insult reshapes brain maturation remains poorly defined. Here, we used a live influenza A virus model of maternal immune activation (MIA) to examine whether prenatal infection alters offspring brain development across adolescence. Pregnant mice were infected at embryonic day 12, and offspring underwent longitudinal high-field MRI at 5, 8, 11 and 14 weeks, followed by prepulse inhibition (PPI) testing as a measure of sensorimotor gating. Maternal influenza exposure produced sex- and age-dependent alterations in brain maturation. Atlas-based volumetry identified FDR-corrected sex- and age-dependent treatment-related effects in the hippocampal CA1 region, while tensor-based morphometry revealed dynamic structural changes across sensory cortices, insula, hippocampus and thalamus. Network analyses further showed disrupted inter-regional structural coordination, particularly in males during early–mid adolescence. Despite partial normalisation of network architecture by late adolescence, influenza-exposed offspring displayed impaired PPI. Partial least squares regression linked these behavioural deficits to altered developmental trajectories in somatosensory cortex, medulla and pons. These findings show that maternal influenza infection does not simply produce static brain abnormalities but alters the trajectory and coordination of adolescent brain maturation in a sex-, region- and circuit-specific manner with long-term behavioural consequences. This work identifies developmental windows and neural systems that may guide future strategies to prevent or reverse infection-associated neurodevelopmental vulnerability.

Introduction Neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD), likely arise from altered developmental trajectories beginning prenatally, when the foetal brain is sensitive to genetic, immune and environmental cues1,2. Although these disorders are highly heritable3, genetics alone cannot account for their onset, timing or clinical heterogeneity4. The prenatal period represents a critical window, when factors like maternal infection and inflammation may act to shape later neuropsychiatric trajectories and outcomes5–7, including influenza virus-related immune activation increasing the risk for schizophrenia-related outcomes8. However, the biological events linking a transient maternal immune challenge to long-term changes in offspring brain maturation remain difficult to resolve in humans. Preclinical models therefore provide an essential platform to identify vulnerable developmental windows, circuits and behaviours that are most vulnerable to disruption from early insults, without the ethical concern as in human study9,10. Maternal immune activation (MIA) provides a powerful experimental framework to model how infection or inflammation during pregnancy alters offspring brain development11. Traditionally, MIA has been induced using immune mimetics such as polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid [poly(I:C)], lipopolysaccharide (LPS), or inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-612,13. These approaches establish that maternal immune responses can disrupt neurodevelopment without direct foetal infection12,13. However, immune mimetics capture only part of the biology of maternal infection. In contrast, live influenza A virus (IAV) engages viral sensing pathways, antiviral immunity, cytokine induction, antibody responses and systemic maternal pathology, including inflammatory and vascular dysfunction14,15. This distinction is critical, because clinically relevant maternal viral infection is not a single immune signal, but a coordinated and dynamic host response. Live-virus MIA models may therefore better represent how maternal infection reshapes foetal and postnatal brain development15. Longitudinal neuroimaging can reveal how prenatal immune challenge alters trajectories of brain maturation16,17, where MIA effects may emerge, evolve or partially normalise across adolescence16. Structural MRI enables repeated, non-invasive assessment of regional brain growth, and tensor-based morphometry (TBM) can quantify both anatomically defined and spatially localised brain changes. The hippocampus is of particular interest because of its role in learning, memory and spatial navigation, has well-established involvement in schizophrenia and related disorders18–21, and is implicated in MIA-associated brain pathology22,23. Longitudinal analysis of its subfields may therefore identify specific time-variant disruptions rather than a whole-region measure. To understand the mechanistic bridge between prenatal immune challenge and later-emerging abnormalities, prepulse inhibition (PPI) provides a behavioural readout of sensorimotor gating, which is disrupted in schizophrenia and other neurodevelopmental disorders24. PPI deficits occur in both human cohorts with schizophrenia and pre-clinical MIA models, including our previous work showing impaired PPI in IAV-infected dams24–26. However, most studies have treated PPI and other behaviours as endpoint phenotypes, with limited insight into the developmental brain trajectories that give rise to impairment. Linking longitudinal MRI to PPI can identify the regions and maturational patterns associated with impaired sensorimotor gating after prenatal viral immune challenge. Here, we leveraged a clinically relevant live IAV model of MIA to determine how prenatal viral immune challenge alters offspring brain maturation across adolescence. Pregnant mice were infected at embryonic day 12, and offspring underwent longitudinal high-field MRI at 5, 8, 11 and 14 weeks, followed by PPI testing in early adulthood. We combined atlas-based segmentation, longitudinal tensor-based morphometry, inter-regional structural correlation network analysis and partial least squares (PLS) regression to define how maternal IAV exposure affects regional brain growth, local morphometry, network organisation and structure–behaviour relationships. We focused particularly on sex-specific effects, given the known sex bias in neurodevelopmental vulnerability following prenatal immune challenge. This design allows us to move beyond static endpoint measures to test whether maternal influenza disrupts the tempo of adolescent brain maturation, creating circuit-level vulnerabilities that persist as impaired sensorimotor gating. Materials and Methods Animals and maternal influenza infection All animal experiments were conducted at the Baker Institute Animal Facility (PAC) and Imaging Facility in Melbourne, Australia, in accordance with the National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) of Australia guidelines for animal experimentation and with approval from Animal Ethics Committee of the Monash Institute of Pharmaceutical Sciences (AEC# 29379). C57BL/6J breeding mice were obtained from the Monash Animal Research Platform and acclimatised for 7 days before time-mating. Females were paired with males at a 1:1 ratio. Mice were housed under a 12 h light/dark cycle at 22°C and 40–60% humidity, with standard chow and water available ad libitum. Plugged dams were housed individually in micro-isolator cages. Mouse-adapted HKx31 influenza A virus (IAV; H3N2) was propagated in 10-day- old embryonated chicken eggs. Viral titres were quantified by plaque assay using Madin-Darby Canine Kidney cells, as previously described27, and virus stocks were stored at −80°C. At embryonic day 12 (E12) of pregnancy, dams were anesthetised with isoflurane and randomly allocated to either the IAV group or phosphate buffered saline (PBS) control group in a balanced 1:1 design (n = 4 dams per group). Dams received intranasal inoculation with either 35μl of 103 PFU IAV or PBS as previously described27. This dose and gestational timing were selected because they induce MIA while minimising offspring lethality15. Maternal body weight was recorded daily from E12 to E16, after which dams were left undisturbed until delivery at approximately E19–E20. Offspring were weaned at 3–3.5 weeks of age and group-housed by sex, with 2–5 mice per cage, under reverse light-cycle conditions. Following completion of behavioural testing, mice were rested for 2–3 days and then euthanised by cervical dislocation. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) acquisition Longitudinal in vivo MRI was performed at 5 (early adolescence), 8 (mid adolescence), 11 (late adolescence) and 14 (early adulthood) weeks of age using a 9.4T small-animal MRI scanner with a mouse room-temperature surface coil (Bruker, USA). Immediately before scanning, mice were anaesthetised using 5% isoflurane in 0.5 – 1L/min in medical grade oxygen and positioned in an MRI compatible animal holder with anaesthesia maintained via a nose cone. Isoflurane concentration was adjusted throughout scanning to maintain stable anaesthesia. Respiratory rate was monitored via a pressure sensor and maintained within 45 – 70 breaths per minute. Body temperature was monitored using a rectal probe and maintained at 37°C with a purpose-built circulating hot-water warming system. Multi-echo gradient echo (GRE) scans were acquired with the following parameters: echo time (TE) 2.1 ms; inter-echo spacing (dTE) 3.1 ms, 12 echoes; Repetition Time (TR) 66 ms; matrix size 174x144x80; Field of View (FOV) 17.4x14.4x8 mm^3; voxel size 100 x 100 x 100 μm3; and four repetitions. *Figure 1 here* Atlas-based volumetric analysis Multi-echo T2*-weighted images were corrected for bias-field inhomogeneity using N4ITK and averaged across echoes to improve anatomical contrast28. Brain extraction was performed using Brain Extraction Net, which was first fine-tuned using existing skull-stripped mouse MRI data and then applied to the full dataset29. The ANTs software toolkit28 was used for volumetric analysis to create group-specific templates for each treatment and sex at each time point, which were then merged to form a comprehensive study template. This study template underwent nonlinear registration to the Allen Mouse Brain CCFv3 using AIDAmri based on NiftyReg, enabling us to accurately segment brain areas (including hippocampal subfields)28,30,31. Nonlinear registrations were applied from individual subject images to the study template for precise region of interest delineation. Manual adjustments were made where necessary on the study template mask. Finally, each region volume was determined by counting the number of voxels it contained. A linear mixed-effects model was employed in MATLAB using the ‘fitlme’ function to investigate the interaction of treatment group, sex, and age on brain region volumes longitudinally. Random effects included intercepts for individual animals and fixed effects for treatment, sex, and age, with age modelled using linear, quadratic and cubic terms. Model residuals were tested for normality using a Q-Q plot and histogram overlaying a standard normal distribution, in addition to using the Lilliefors test for normality corroboration. This model accounted for the fixed effects of treatment group, sex, and age, as well as their interactions up to the cubic term for age, thereby effectively handling longitudinal repeated measures data. P-values from the atlas-based volumetric analysis were corrected for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Tensor-Based Morphometry (TBM) Tensor-based morphometry was used to assess localised differences in brain morphology across development. Aligned raw data from each individual were initially registered to a Minimum Deformation Template (MDT) created from PBS images. Non-linear registrations of individuals to MDT were performed to obtain the absolute Jacobian determinants, ensuring local anatomical variations were captured and facilitating exact comparison of morphological differences across individuals. Following registration, deformation fields from each individual data to the MDT were analysed by the log Jacobian determinant, providing a voxel-wise representation of local volume changes rate (expansion or contraction) relative to the MDT. Statistical analysis of TBM data was completed using linear mixed effects model — voxel-wise models were used to examine treatment group, sex, and age effects while accounting for longitudinal data structure. Fixed effects included treatment group, sex, and age, together with their interactions. Random effects included individual intercepts. A permutation (5000 times random shuffling of treatment and sex labels) approach for correction in multiple comparisons was used for data analysis. At each permutation, clusters of voxels with statistical significance greater than |t| > 3 were identified, and the maximum sum of the t-statistic over voxels in each cluster was taken. Significant threshold p-values were thus identified using the resulting distribution of maximum sums under the null. Graph theoretical analysis of inter-regional structural correlations Graph theoretical analyses were used to examine whether maternal IAV exposure altered the coordination of regional brain growth across development. For each sex and treatment group, Spearman’s rank correlation matrices were generated from longitudinal changes in regional brain volumes. Correlations were calculated between all pairs of brain regions using percentage volume change across consecutive imaging intervals: 5–8 weeks, 8–11 weeks, and 11– 14 weeks. This approach allowed us to assess whether regional brain maturation occurred in a coordinated or disrupted manner across development. Correlation matrices were thresholded at Spearman’s ρ = 0.625 to retain robust inter-regional associations while reducing the influence of weak or potentially spurious correlations. Network organisation was then assessed using graph theoretical metrics, including Jaccard similarity index, characteristic path length, assortativity, closeness centrality and transitivity. Jaccard similarity was used to quantify the similarity of network architecture between treatment groups, characteristic path length to assess global network integration, assortativity to determine whether nodes preferentially connected with other nodes of similar degree, closeness centrality to estimate nodal communication efficiency, and transitivity to assess local clustering. Community structure was examined using the Louvain method. Prepulse inhibition (PPI) testing Prepulse inhibition test was conducted 3-4 days after the final MRI scan at 14 weeks of age. Mice underwent a mock PPI session for habituation, followed by the test session 24 h later, as described previously15,25. Two-way ANOVA was conducted to examine main effects of treatment (PBS vs. IAV) and sex, and their interactions, followed by post hoc analyses where appropriate. Structure–behaviour modelling Partial least squares (PLS) regression was used to explore correlations between structural brain developmental trajectory parameters (intercept, 1st, 2nd, 3rd order coefficients) and behavioural performance in the PPI test. Merritt1, K.H. Christopher Choy2, Stella Liong3, Robert Brkljača4, Cassandra M.J. Wannan5, Ulysse M.C.C. Thivisol1, David K. Corresponding author: Professor Christos Pantelis Department of Psychiatry, The University of Melbourne Melbourne, VIC, Australia Email: cpant@unimelb.edu.au Abstract Maternal infection during pregnancy is increasingly recognised as a risk factor for neurodevelopmental disorders, yet how a clinically relevant viral insult reshapes brain maturation remains poorly defined. Here, we used a live influenza A virus model of maternal immune activation (MIA) to examine whether prenatal infection alters offspring brain development across adolescence. Pregnant mice were infected at embryonic day 12, and offspring underwent longitudinal high-field MRI at 5, 8, 11 and 14 weeks, followed by prepulse inhibition (PPI) testing as a measure of sensorimotor gating. Maternal influenza exposure produced sex- and age-dependent alterations in brain maturation. Atlas-based volumetry identified FDR-corrected sex- and age- dependent treatment-related effects in the hippocampal CA1 region, while tensor-based morphometry revealed dynamic structural changes across sensory cortices, insula, hippocampus and thalamus. Network analyses further showed disrupted inter-regional structural coordination, particularly in males during early–mid adolescence. Despite partial normalisation of network architecture by late adolescence, influenza-exposed offspring displayed impaired PPI. Partial least squares regression linked these behavioural deficits to altered developmental trajectories in somatosensory cortex, medulla and pons. These findings show that maternal influenza infection does not simply produce static brain abnormalities but alters the trajectory and coordination of adolescent brain maturation in a sex-, region- and circuit-specific manner with long-term behavioural consequences. This work identifies developmental windows and neural systems that may guide future strategies to prevent or reverse infection-associated neurodevelopmental vulnerability. Introduction Neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD), likely arise from altered developmental trajectories beginning prenatally, when the foetal brain is sensitive to genetic, immune and environmental cues1,2. Although these disorders are highly heritable3, genetics alone cannot account for their onset, timing or clinical heterogeneity4. The prenatal period represents a critical window, when factors like maternal infection and inflammation may act to shape later neuropsychiatric trajectories and outcomes5–7, including influenza virus-related immune activation increasing the risk for schizophrenia-related outcomes8. However, the biological events linking a transient maternal immune challenge to long-term changes in offspring brain maturation remain difficult to resolve in humans. Preclinical models therefore provide an essential platform to identify vulnerable developmental windows, circuits and behaviours that are most vulnerable to disruption from early insults, without the ethical concern as in human study9,10. Maternal immune activation (MIA) provides a powerful experimental framework to model how infection or inflammation during pregnancy alters offspring brain development11. Traditionally, MIA has been induced using immune mimetics such as polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid [poly(I:C)], lipopolysaccharide (LPS), or inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-612,13. These approaches establish that maternal immune responses can disrupt neurodevelopment without direct foetal infection12,13. However, immune mimetics capture only part of the biology of maternal infection. In contrast, live influenza A virus (IAV) engages viral sensing pathways, antiviral immunity, cytokine induction, antibody responses and systemic maternal pathology, including inflammatory and vascular dysfunction14,15. This distinction is critical, because clinically relevant maternal viral infection is not a single immune signal, but a coordinated and dynamic host response. Live-virus MIA models may therefore better represent how maternal infection reshapes foetal and postnatal brain development15. Longitudinal neuroimaging can reveal how prenatal immune challenge alters trajectories of brain maturation16,17, where MIA effects may emerge, evolve or partially normalise across adolescence16. Structural MRI enables repeated, non-invasive assessment of regional brain growth, and tensor-based morphometry (TBM) can quantify both anatomically defined and spatially localised brain changes. The hippocampus is of particular interest because of its role in learning, memory and spatial navigation, has well-established involvement in schizophrenia and related disorders18–21, and is implicated in MIA-associated brain pathology22,23. Longitudinal analysis of its subfields may therefore identify specific time-variant disruptions rather than a whole-region measure. To understand the mechanistic bridge between prenatal immune challenge and later-emerging abnormalities, prepulse inhibition (PPI) provides a behavioural readout of sensorimotor gating, which is disrupted in schizophrenia and other neurodevelopmental disorders24. PPI deficits occur in both human cohorts with schizophrenia and pre-clinical MIA models, including our previous work showing impaired PPI in IAV-infected dams24–26. However, most studies have treated PPI and other behaviours as endpoint phenotypes, with limited insight into the developmental brain trajectories that give rise to impairment. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of maternal influenza infection on adolescent brain maturation and sensorimotor gating in mice. The research highlights that prenatal exposure to influenza A virus leads to sex- and age-dependent changes in brain development, particularly affecting males during early to mid-adolescence. Using longitudinal MRI and PPI testing, the study identifies altered developmental trajectories in specific brain regions, suggesting long-term behavioural consequences. These findings contribute to understanding how viral insults during pregnancy can influence neurodevelopmental processes, offering insights into potential targets for intervention. However, the study's results are based on a single model of maternal immune activation, which may limit generalisability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on animal models and the absence of direct human data.

abstract_zh: 人们越来越认识到,怀孕期间的母亲感染是神经发育障碍的危险因素,但临床相关的病毒损伤如何重塑大脑成熟仍不清楚。在这里,我们使用母体免疫激活(MIA)的活甲型流感病毒模型来检查产前感染是否会改变后代整个青春期的大脑发育。怀孕小鼠在胚胎第 12 天被感染,后代在第 5、8、11 和 14 周时接受纵向高场 MRI,随后进行前脉冲抑制 (PPI) 测试作为感觉运动门控的测量。母亲接触流感会导致大脑成熟度发生性别和年龄依赖性改变。基于图集的体积测定确定了海马 CA1 区域中 FDR 校正的性别和年龄依赖性 治疗 相关效应,而基于张量的形态测量则揭示了感觉皮层、岛叶、海马和丘脑的动态结构变化。网络分析进一步显示区域间结构协调被破坏,特别是在青春期早期至中期的男性中。尽管网络结构在青春期后期部分正常化,但暴露于流感的后代表现出 PPI 受损。偏最小二乘回归将这些行为缺陷与体感皮层、髓质和脑桥的发育轨迹改变联系起来。这些发现表明,孕产妇流感感染不仅仅会产生静态的大脑异常,还会以性别、区域和回路特异性的方式改变青少年大脑成熟的轨迹和协调,从而产生长期的行为后果。这项工作确定了发育窗口和神经系统,可以指导未来预防或逆转感染相关神经发育脆弱性的策略。

title: Newton Divided Difference Optimization for Fingerprint-Based Neural Virtual Screening against Avian Influenza A/H9N2
abstract: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening. This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization, a lightweight positive diagonal curvature-aware training strategy, as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols. An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds. NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteriztic – Area Under the Curve) and PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve) on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance. The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings, although external validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization.

title: Early oseltamivir initiation and influenza outcomes in kidney transplant recipients: a multicenter real-world study
abstract: Influenza infection poses a significant clinical threat to kidney transplant recipients due to their immunocompromised status. Although current guidelines recommend early antiviral therapy, real-world evidence supporting the effectiveness of oseltamivir, particularly regarding the optimal timing of initiation in this vulnerable population remains scarce. To identify independent factors associated with clinical improvement and time to symptom resolution in kidney transplant recipients infected with the influenza virus and treated with oseltamivir. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study enrolling adult kidney transplant recipients diagnosed with influenza virus infection across five centers between October 2023 and March 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using a validated Composite Symptom Score (range: 0–21) based on seven typical influenza symptoms. Clinical improvement was defined as achieving a score of ≤ 1 on the fifth day after oseltamivir initiation. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with clinical improvement, and linear regression was used to evaluate factors influencing time to symptom resolution. Given the small number of events, the multivariable logistic model was estimated using Firth’s penalized likelihood method and restricted to two core predictors. A total of 58 kidney transplant recipients were included. After one course of oseltamivir, 46 patients (79.3%) achieved clinical improvement. Compared with the improved group, patients without improvement had a significantly lower rate of early oseltamivir initiation (≤ 48 h: 58.3% vs. 84.8%, P = 0.044) and tended to present with higher baseline symptom scores. In multivariable logistic regression, oseltamivir initiation > 48 h was the only factor independently and significantly associated with reduced likelihood of clinical improvement (adjusted OR = 0.16, 95% CI: 0.03–0.76, P = 0.030), after adjusting for onset symptom score using Firth’s penalized likelihood logistic regression to account for the small number of events. Higher baseline onset symptom score was also significantly associated with unfavorable outcomes (adjusted OR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.63–0.91, P = 0.007). Consistently, multivariable linear regression confirmed that late oseltamivir initiation was independently associated with prolonged time to symptom resolution (β = 5.02, 95% CI: 3.00–7.04, P < 0.001). Neither dosage adjustment nor treatment duration extension was significantly associated with clinical outcomes. In this multicenter real-world study, early oseltamivir initiation (≤ 48 h) was the strongest independent predictor of both clinical improvement and a shorter symptom resolution time in kidney transplant recipients with influenza. Baseline disease severity showed a trend-level association with unfavorable outcomes, suggesting a narrowing “window of opportunity” for a therapeutic response in patients with a higher symptom burden. These findings reinforce the critical importance of prompt antiviral intervention in immunocompromised transplant recipients and provide real-world evidence to support clinical decision-making for early treatment prioritization.

analysis.summary_en: This multicenter retrospective study evaluated the impact of early oseltamivir initiation on clinical outcomes in 58 kidney transplant recipients with influenza across five centers from October 2023 to March 2024. Using a validated Composite Symptom Score, 79.3% of patients achieved clinical improvement after treatment, with early initiation (≤ 48 hours) independently associated with higher odds of improvement (adjusted OR 0.16) and shorter symptom resolution (β 5.02). Late treatment initiation and higher baseline severity were linked to poorer outcomes. Consistently, multivariable linear regression confirmed that late oseltamivir initiation was independently associated with prolonged time to symptom resolution (β = 5.02, 95% CI: 3.00–7.04, P < 0.001). Neither dosage adjustment nor treatment duration extension was significantly associated with clinical outcomes. In this multicenter real-world study, early oseltamivir initiation (≤ 48 h) was the strongest independent predictor of both clinical improvement and a shorter symptom resolution time in kidney transplant recipients with influenza. Baseline disease severity showed a trend-level association with unfavorable outcomes, suggesting a narrowing “window of opportunity” for a therapeutic response in patients with a higher symptom burden. These findings reinforce the critical importance of prompt antiviral intervention in immunocompromised transplant recipients and provide real-world evidence to support clinical decision-making for early treatment prioritization.

title: Recent advances in emerging approaches for influenza a detection
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a major focus of global public health concern, as it can cause influenza-like illness and severe respiratory infections. Therefore, achieving accurate and sensitive detection of IAV would greatly facilitate disease diagnosis and control. The two main conventional technical methods for IAV detection that are reviewed in this article are viral nucleic acid amplification analysis and immunological assays. At the same time, this review pays special attention to the cross-integration of these two types of techniques with modern engineering technologies, and systematically introduces novel biosensors (offering significantly enhanced sensitivity) and point-of-care testing (POCT) devices (enabling rapid on-site diagnosis) developed based on these two principles. However, it is important to note that the majority of these novel platforms remain at the proof-of-concept stage, with validation largely confined to laboratory settings. By delineating the current state of these technologies, this review identifies key challenges and future directions for translating research innovations into clinical practice.
